usageNotes: Use this to inspect the full configuration of a specific network interface on a PDM node, including IP addressing, interface type, bond/bridge membership, and active state. Requires System.Audit privilege on the specific interface path. The response reflects the on-disk /etc/network/interfaces configuration, not necessarily the live kernel state — check the 'active' field to confirm the interface is currently UP.

examples.summary: Read configuration for the management bridge vmbr0 on node pdm1

tips: The 'active' field reflects kernel UP state; 'autostart' reflects whether the interface is configured to come up at boot — both can differ after manual ifup/ifdown.
For VLAN interfaces, expect 'vlan-id' and 'vlan-raw-device' fields in the response; for bonds, expect 'bond_mode' and 'slaves'.
Interface names are capped at 15 characters (Linux IFNAMSIZ limit), which also applies to the iface path parameter.
This endpoint reads the pending configuration file. If changes have been made but not applied, the response may differ from what is currently active on the node.
